# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have learned from the manual that the required action is to cut the white wire. Since I cannot speak, I am signaling this to Deaf, who can relay the instruction verbally to Blind. I use an open hand to suggest “white” and a pinching gesture to suggest “cut.”

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile facts: strip has three engraved marks in pattern A-B-A. A is an unfamiliar mark shaped roughly like an upside-down T. B is a different unfamiliar compact rounded mark. Keypad by position: 1=2, 2=9, 3=0, 4=8; entered nothing. Display, light, and wires 1-6 reveal nothing tactile. Use the manual and tell me the required press or cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb state: display 6. Light red. Painted strip blue yellow blue. Keypad engraved 1 maps to 2, 2 maps to 9, 3 maps to 0, 4 maps to 8. It says 1 digit; entered nothing. Wires: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Consult the manual and tell Blind the exact safe action.

The manual still requires cutting the white wire. Deaf’s view identifies the white wire as wire 2, so I am sending Deaf the established gesture for white, followed by two, then cut. Deaf can state the exact action to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✌", "🤏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Update: light is now yellow; display 6, strip blue yellow blue, keypad mappings 1 to 2, 2 to 9, 3 to 0, 4 to 8, one digit required and none entered, wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. I cannot interpret the gestures without a code. Please read the manual and speak the exact safe action to Blind.

The safe action remains cutting wire 2, because the manual says to cut the white wire and Deaf identifies white as wire 2. Since Deaf cannot hear and I cannot speak, I can only resend a compact visual instruction: two, then cut. The keypad and light are irrelevant to this manual instruction.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤏"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please relay the manual's exact required action now: either press slot 1-4 or cut wire position 1-6, including any condition that must be checked. I cannot use the printed strip or colours.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is 1 and light is blue. Strip remains blue yellow blue. Keypad remains 1 maps to 2, 2 to 9, 3 to 0, 4 to 8; one digit required, none entered. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please relay the manual's exact safe action to Blind.

The manual gives an unconditional instruction: cut the white wire. Deaf’s bomb view identifies the white wire as position 2. I cannot speak or reach Blind, so I must send Deaf the visual instruction for white, wire 2, and cut; Deaf can then say the exact action aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✌", "🤏"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No message has arrived. I need the manual's final command: press slot 1, 2, 3, or 4, or cut wire 1 through 6. Please send only the exact operation and number.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display 7, light green. Strip blue yellow blue. Keypad: 1 maps to 2, 2 to 9, 3 to 0, 4 to 8; one digit required, none entered. Wires: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please use the manual and tell Blind the exact safe action now.

The required operation is unconditional: cut wire 2, because the manual says to cut the white wire and Deaf confirms that wire 2 is white. I will send Deaf the established visual shorthand for cut followed by the number 2, so Deaf can relay it to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no manual result. Send the literal final action immediately, formatted exactly as press slot N or cut position N, with N from the permitted range.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 1, light red. Strip blue yellow blue. Keypad: 1 maps to 2, 2 to 9, 3 to 0, 4 to 8; one digit required, none entered. Wires: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please immediately read the manual and speak the exact safe action to Blind.

The final action is to cut wire 2. I cannot speak to Blind; Deaf is the only channel that can receive my gesture and then voice the instruction to Blind. I am sending the operation and wire number directly to Deaf.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No instruction has arrived after six turns. Please send the exact safe operation now; otherwise I must continue waiting.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 9, light green. Strip blue yellow blue. Keypad: 1 maps to 2, 2 to 9, 3 to 0, 4 to 8; one digit required, none entered. Wires: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Read the manual and speak the exact safe action to Blind now.

The exact safe operation is **cut wire 2**. I cannot speak to Blind, so the only available relay is Deaf: I am sending the operation first, then the wire number, using the same visual shorthand.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "✌"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 6, light blue. Strip blue yellow blue. Keypad: 1 maps to 2, 2 to 9, 3 to 0, 4 to 8; one digit required, none entered. Wires: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please speak the manual-derived exact safe action directly to Blind now.

The manual’s unconditional command is **cut wire 2**. Deaf is the only one who can see my gestures, so I will send the two-part visual instruction again: cut, then 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "✌"])
```
